title: How much saffron can nine niskas buy in the old problem?
description: An old problem from the Lilavati gives the price of two and a half palas of saffron as three sevenths of a niska. The video finds the factor of change from the old money to nine niskas and scales the saffron by it.
teaching_notes: One idea: the factor of change can be a whole number even when the terms are fractions, found by dividing the new money by the old money. Watch for students who divide by three sevenths and then multiply by the wrong fraction.

video_script.why: The same factor of change works when the terms are fractions, because money and saffron stay in proportion.
video_script.substitution: Divide nine by three sevenths to get the factor, then multiply two and a half by that factor.
video_script.anchor: the old problem from the Lilavati about saffron, palas and niskas, from the book
video_script.payoff_line: The buyer can get fifty two and a half palas of saffron

final_answer.spoken: fifty two and a half palas of saffron

video_script.fraction_reading: three sevenths, seven thirds, two and a half
video_script.design: One idea: one factor of change scales a fraction problem. The old verse stays as a card on the stage, and the money and saffron ratio sits on the board.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book. It is an old problem from the Lilavati.
<bookmark mark='units'/>In those days, weight was measured in palas, and money was measured in niskas.
<bookmark mark='price'/>Two and a half palas of saffron cost three sevenths of a niska.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How much saffron can be bought for nine niskas?

narration: <bookmark mark='double'/>Twice the money buys twice the saffron.
<bookmark mark='same'/>If the money grows by a factor, the saffron grows by the same factor.
<bookmark mark='frac'/>The terms here are fractions, but the idea does not change.

beats.on_screen: Given: 2.5 palas of saffron cost 3/7 niska; money available is 9 niskas

marks.given: the saffron, the price and the money available are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, two and a half palas of saffron cost three sevenths of a niska. We have nine niskas.

beats.on_screen: To find: the saffron for 9 niskas

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the saffron that nine niskas can buy.

marks.prop: 3/7 : 2.5 :: 9 : x is written with money under the first pair

narration: <bookmark mark='prop'/>Step one, write the proportion of money to saffron. Three sevenths is to two and a half as nine is to the missing saffron.

marks.div: 9 ÷ 3/7 is written as the factor of change

narration: <bookmark mark='div'/>Step two, find the factor of change. Divide nine by three sevenths.
<bookmark mark='flip'/>Dividing by three sevenths means multiplying by seven thirds. Nine times seven thirds is sixty three thirds, which is twenty one.
<bookmark mark='mul'/>Step three, multiply the saffron by the same factor. Two and a half times twenty one has two parts.
<bookmark mark='split'/>Twice twenty one is forty two, and half of twenty one is ten and a half. Together they make fifty two and a half.

marks.right: 2.5 × 9 = 22.5 is written and the two are ticked

narration: <bookmark mark='left'/>Step four, check by cross multiplying. Three sevenths of fifty two and a half is twenty two and a half.
<bookmark mark='right'/>Two and a half times nine is also twenty two and a half.

marks.ans: the answer is boxed beside the big coin pile

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The buyer can get fifty two and a half palas of saffron for nine niskas.
